name: confirmation-at-the-reported-anchor
description:
The companion to copy-link-confirmation, and the one that answers the actual question. That scenario shrinks the window to 700px so the confirmation lands clear of the screen's top-right corner, and it proves the bubble paints - but a sceptic can say it only proves the bubble paints SOMEWHERE ELSE, not at the anchor a report photographed. This one takes the window as it comes and measures the corner itself.

A report gave bounds 740,52 262x36 and a blank capture there. Cropping that exact rect out of a full-size frame from this suite returns the macOS '“com.apple.sshd-session” Is Accessing Your Screen' reminder - an OS window at status level, over the top-right corner, covering the anchor completely. The bubble is underneath it, so no capture of those pixels can show the bubble while the banner is up, however correct the rect is.

So the settles here are the measurement, not padding. They exist to outlast the banner's cooldown, and the pixel assertion below only means anything on a run where the banner stayed down. The vlog assertion means something either way, which is the whole argument for having it.

actions.note: CopyCurrentPageLink returns false with no committed contents, so without this the chord is a no-op
cgevent posts to the frontmost app; an ssh-launched Atrium is not it
park the pointer in empty page content. A pointer on a link raises the hover form of this same widget at a different anchor.

outlast the screen-recording banner raised by the probe-tool warm-up capture. The banner lives about five seconds; replayd re-evaluates on every SCStream start but on a cooldown, and this is the window that lets the cooldown lapse before the corner is measured.
the corner at rest, and also the last SCStream before the measured one
and outlast any banner THAT capture raised, so the burst below starts on a quiet corner

On its own, so the poll below can run WHILE the card is up. The burst that follows is for the frames, and a poll after it sees nothing: the card lives CONFIRM_MS and its empty stack box is removed with it.

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t ? t.textContent : ''; })()
actions.note: The card lives on the /toast widget now, not in the sidebar document. Hosted there its top/right resolved against the sidebar's narrow column, so it appeared in that column's upper right rather than the window's - reported twice.
let this card expire so the measured burst starts clean
THE MEASUREMENT, at the untouched default window size - the same geometry that produced the 740,52 262x36 the task quoted.

assertions.label: the-copy-link-path-actually-ran
assertions.note: the control, same as the sibling scenario

assertions.label: the-confirmation-was-shown-at-the-corner
assertions.note: Two, not one: the chord fires once on its own so the poll can catch the card while it is up, and again inside the capture burst for the frames. One would mean a chord went nowhere.

assertions.label: the-card-is-in-the-shared-stack-not-its-own-surface
assertions.desc: the anchor claim is structural now rather than positional - the card is a child of .toasts, the one stack every other toast uses, so it cannot drift to a corner of its own. The old region was the native bubble's and no longer describes anything.
and the window survived the chord
